newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee gains on dollar profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee gains on dollar profit-taking.

text.p: The Sri Lanka rupee strengthened against the U.S. dollar on Tuesday as banks sold the greenback on fears that depreciation of the local currency may have ended, dealers said.
At 0500 GMT the rupee was at 58.85 to the dollar, after opening at 59.13.

"Banks are taking profit and unwinding long dollar positions. They believe today's Central Bank's action could indicate that short-term depreciation targets have been met," said an ABN Amro Bank dealer.
The Central Bank left the dollar-rupee exchange rate unchaged despite overseas gains by the greenback. Buying and selling prices were at 58.2170 and 59.3931.
The Central Bank's recent bullishness towards the greenback and a lack of import, had left banks carrying substantital dollar positions, dealers said.
"If the Central Bank leaves the exchange rate unchanged one more day, we could see the dollar fall close to 58.21," said a Standard Chartered Bank dealer.
Overnight call money was moving between 10 percent and 10.5 percent, dealers said.
